title: Flexible pollution curves did not close the community response gap at 217 English river sites in 1991-2017
abstract: We tested whether curved spatial pollution responses explain weak community change at 217 English river sites. We trained linear and additive natural cubic models on 1991-2000 family-presence vectors and tested held-out spatial calibration and change to 2008-2017. Linear BOD transfer was 0.076. Three flexible models gave 0.129-0.186, with central 95% ranges from joint site and three-year-block resamples that included zero and stayed below 0.33. Flexible curves increased the expected BOD change rather than reducing it. They did not improve conditional temporal prediction. Clipping exposures to training ranges, requiring more endpoint samples, and survey-day adjustment kept small ratios. Thus moderate additive curvature did not close the gap in these records. This is a new benchmark test in a previously used dataset, not an independent survey. It does not exclude abrupt thresholds, interactions, habitat confounding or exposure error, and it does not identify an ecological cause. Code, aggregate results, input hashes and retrieval instructions are included. External records are excluded.

display.caption: Flexible spatial curves kept weak temporal transfer and increased expected pollution-related change. Lines show central 95% resample ranges, not exact confidence limits.
